articles.title: Oil prices climb as traders assess Middle East developments
articles.summary: Oil prices climbed Wednesday as worries over Middle East supply disruptions keep the market on edge, with attacks on tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy facilities denting sentiment. The escalating tensions have also sent global oil shipping costs soaring, adding another layer of pressure to energy markets.

articles.title: Australian data center operator NextDC's shares plunge 40% after it slashes earnings forecast
articles.summary: Shares of Australia's NextDC plunged 39.5% on Wednesday after the data center operator slashed its annual earnings forecast, citing power supply delays at its Melbourne facility amid local community and stakeholder opposition. As Australia grapples with growing concerns over the impact of data center developments on local communities, Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the government was working to establish national standards for investment.

articles.title: Elice's huge stock swings show AI's spending boom is getting more investor scrutiny
articles.summary: A bruising stock market debut by South Korean AI infrastructure provider Elice has become the latest warning sign that investors may be more closely scrutinizing ambitious expansion plans and paths to profitability. The shift is particularly significant for Asia, where technology markets are heavily exposed to the semiconductor and memory-chip industries that have powered the global AI investment frenzy.

articles.title: Japan exports post huge miss in September as growth slows to 16.7%
articles.summary: Growth was supported by continued strong semiconductor exports, with shipments rising 49.4% year on year by value. Exports of machinery also bolstered growth, with semiconductor-related machinery shipments up 43.9% and power generation machinery exports climbing 22.6%. Exports have been the main driver of Japan's growth for the first two quarters of 2026, helping the world's fourth largest economy beat expectations in the first quarter, and supporting growth in the second.

articles.title: Obsessed with CoreWeave and the AI trade? You're missing out on some great stocks
articles.summary: Good news like a reversal in oil prices after a big spike, or a robust bond market driven by a frozen housing market, as mortgage rates are too high for most to afford a house. Or, in terms of "you haven't missed it yet," check out the reaction in GE Aerospace's stock to its 49% order growth. Tuesday's earnings show there's a cohort of the market that can thrive outside of the AI and data-center trade.

articles.title: United Airlines slashes 2026 profit outlook on fuel prices, but travelers keep booking despite higher fares
articles.summary: United Airlines is slashing its profit forecast for the year as fuel costs continue to bite, but the carrier said passengers keep booking. United said Tuesday that it expects to earn between 50 cents and $1.50 a share on an adjusted basis in the fourth quarter, well below the $1.76 a share Wall Street analysts expected. At the high end of that range, it would bring United's 2026 adjusted earnings to no more than $7.22 per share.

articles.title: Housing is flashing warning signs just as the Fed weighs more interest rate hikes
articles.summary: Housing data deteriorated further in September, according to separate reports Tuesday, adding to an already complicated policy landscape for the central bank as it contemplates its next move on interest rates. Fed officials have said they are tracking the inflationary effects of the robust investment in artificial intelligence, which is driving up the cost of chips and electronics.

articles.title: Trump sued over 50% tariffs on Canada in latest trade challenge
articles.summary: Trump in July used Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to slap those steep tariffs on Canadian hockey sticks, wine, honey, wigs, and other products in response to alleged trade discrimination by Ottawa. It was the first time the 96-year-old law had ever been used to impose a tariff. It says that the law permits tariff action "only upon finding 'as a fact'" that a foreign country is unequally imposing unreasonable charges or trade limitations on U.S.

articles.title: What options traders expect from SpaceX earnings after the bell
articles.summary: The company delivered four astronauts to the International Space Station in record time, expanded its mobile network spectrum, is reportedly eyeing a $40 billion debt deal to buy Nvidia chips, and CEO Elon Musk said he plans to give shares to every kid in America next year. Traders think all that means more gains for the stock after it reports earnings after the bell Tuesday.
